{{legend0|#808080|TBD result}} {{legend0|#FFDC43|TBD in runoff}} }} The '''2026 United States House of Representatives elections''' were held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, as part of the [[2026 United States elections|2026 midterm elections]] during President [[Donald Trump]]'s [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|second, nonconsecutive term]]. Voters elected representatives from all 435 [[List of United States congressional districts|congressional districts]] across each of the fifty [[U.S. state]]s, and five of the six [[Non-voting members of the United States House of Representatives|non-voting delegates]] from the [[Washington, D.C.|District of Columbia]] and the inhabited [[Insular area|U.S. territories]]. Special elections are also being held on dates throughout 2026. Other federal, state, and local elections, including [[2026 United States Senate elections|elections to the Senate]], were also held on November 3, 2026. The winners of this election will serve in the [[120th United States Congress]] in January 3, 2027, with seats apportioned among the states based on the [[2020 United States census]] and revised district maps as a result of the [[2025–2026 United States redistricting]]. Primary elections were held between March 3 and September 15, 2026. Democrats won a majority for the first time since [[2020 U.S. House of Representatives elections|2020]]. With two districts going to a runoff ([[Louisiana's 5th congressional district|LA-05]] and [[Louisiana's 6th congressional district|LA-06]]),{{efn|The [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Louisiana]] were held using a [[jungle primary]] system to give state legislators time to redraw congressional maps following the ''[[Louisiana v. In 2026, most states used the same districts created in the [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|redistricting cycle following the 2020 census]], which were first used in the 2022 elections. Maps have changed or would change in several states, often due to legal challenges made based on partisan or racial [[Gerrymandering in the United States|gerrymandering]]. In April 2026, the Supreme Court ruled on ''[[Louisiana v. Callais]]'' that stricter scrutiny had to be applied with regard to section 2 of the [[Voting Rights Act]]. {{Table alignment}} === Legal challenges to current maps === Several states had legal Redistricting was transferred from the General Assembly to a bipartisan commission in [[2020 Virginia Question 1|2020]], and the power would revert to the commission for the normal 2030 cycle.
